cards.title: Daily discount applied to prices and shown as a banner
cards.summary: A discount whose inclusive date range covers today reduces the displayed price by its size, formatted to two decimals, and shows a banner with the rounded percentage and end date. Six seeded discounts from September to December 2017 range from 10% to 50%.

claims.text: The service returns the first discount whose start and end dates (compared by day) include the requested day.
The displayed price is the price multiplied by (1 minus the discount size), formatted with two decimals.
The banner reads '<percent>% sale endson <end date>!', with the percent rounded to a whole number.
The seeded discounts are six fixed date ranges in September, October, November and December 2017, with sizes from 10% to 50%.

cards.title: Stock record is one row per item and date
cards.summary: Saving stock for an item and date overwrites the existing quantity for that day, or inserts a new row with the next id when none exists. The live service reports zero stock for a day with no row, while the mock service's GetAvailableStock fails when no row matches.

claims.text: If a stock record exists for the same item and date, its AvailableStock is replaced by the new value and saved.
Otherwise a new stock record is inserted with the next StockId (maximum plus one).
The CatalogItemsStock record holds AvailableStock, CatalogItemId, Date and StockId fields.
Stock is matched by item id and calendar date, ignoring the time part.

cards.title: CatalogItem (product entity, legacy and modernized)
cards.summary: A sellable catalog product with an id, a name (max 50), an optional description, a price (decimal, money), a picture file name (default dummy.png), required links to one brand and one type, and stock figures (available stock, restock threshold, max stock threshold) plus an on-reorder flag. In the legacy EF model it is the CatalogItems set; in the modernized model it is the Catalog table. PictureUri and TempImageName are not stored. Ids are assigned by the application (hi-lo or sequence) or by the seed, and the foreign keys cascade deletes by EF default in some versions.

claims.text: The context exposes five sets: CatalogBrands, CatalogItems, CatalogItemsStocks, CatalogTypes and DiscountItems.
CatalogItem.Id is not database generated; Price is money with precision 19,4 and Picturefilename holds the image file name.
DiscountItem has Size as double, Start and End as date columns, and Id as the key.
The brand and type names are stored as non-Unicode strings.

cards.title: Browse the catalog with brand and type filters
cards.summary: The catalog screen lists items with thumbnails, names, descriptions and prices, and filters them by brand and type. Changing either filter reloads the grid, with 0 meaning All. Thumbnails are read from the Assets/Images/Catalog folder.

claims.text: On load, the controller shows the discount banner, loads all items, loads the brand and type filter lists and loads the shipment view.
The brand and type dropdowns each raise a filter change with the selected ids, and the controller reloads the grid for that filter. Id 0 means All.
The dropdown change handlers are wired in the designer for the brand and type combo boxes.
Each row shows a 384x216 thumbnail loaded from the Assets/Images/Catalog folder under the current directory, the item id, name and description, and the price prefixed with $.

cards.title: Open the catalog screen

claims.text: Main creates the catalog view and a service client, wires them into the controller, and calls LoadView before showing the dialog.

cards.title: Switch between mock data and the real catalog database
cards.summary: A UseMockData setting chooses between in-memory mock data and the real SQL Server catalog database. It is set in Web.config, in the container override files, or in the legacy app settings, and it also decides whether the database context or initializer is registered.

claims.text: The MVC and WebForms apps can connect to the real database or use mock data when the database is unavailable, for testing or demos.
The containerised WebForms app also sets UseMockData=False.
The containerised MVC app sets UseMockData=False in its compose override, and the flag is read by CatalogConfiguration.UseMockData, which the application uses to choose its data path.
The UseMockData setting is read as a boolean; the shipped appsettings.json sets it to the string "true".

cards.title: Template parameter defaults, allowed values and load-balanced ports
cards.summary: The cluster templates set defaults for node ports, network ranges, VM image and 30 load-balanced application ports. They also limit the public IP type, the certificate store, the protection level and the storage replication options to listed values.

claims.text: publicIPAddressType allows only the value Dynamic and defaults to Dynamic.
The subnet defaults to 10.0.0.0/24, the virtual network address space to 10.0.0.0/16, and overProvision to the string false.
The node port defaults are application 20000-30000, ephemeral 49152-65534, and gateway ports 19000 (TCP), 19080 (HTTP) and 19081 (reverse proxy).
Thirty load-balanced application ports are defaulted, including 5114, 5433, 80 to 85, 88, 8080, 8888, 1433, 443, 5100 to 5110, 5112, 5113, 5115, 15672, 5672 and 6379.

cards.title: Catalog item entity (Catalog table and CatalogItem class)
cards.summary: The Catalog table and the CatalogItem class hold one row per sellable product with an int identity-like Id (application-assigned via hi-lo generator), name, description, price, picture file name, brand and type foreign keys, and stock fields (AvailableStock, RestockThreshold, MaxStockThreshold, OnReorder). Services eager-load CatalogBrand and CatalogType navigation properties. PictureUri is not stored. Column nullability, length and precision details vary slightly by source.

claims.text: Column Catalog.Id: int, NOT NULL, identity (SQL Server IdentityColumn), primary key (PK_Catalog).
Column Catalog.Name: nvarchar (string) max length 50, NOT NULL.
Column Catalog.Description: string, NULL.
Column Catalog.Price: decimal, NOT NULL, no precision given in the migration.

cards.title: Back-office catalog maintenance in the MVC and WebForms sample apps
cards.summary: The README describes two sample web apps for the internal back office of an eShop, where employees update the product catalog.

answeredQuestions.question: What is the specific logic within CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue to generate the CatalogItem ID?
answeredQuestions.answer: HiLo: when the block is used up it runs SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR catalog_hilo (a SQL Server sequence) and then hands out the next 9 ids from memory (HiLoIncrement = 10), under a lock (eShopLegacyMVC/Models/CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.cs:11-30).
